text:
lina: Heads-up — canary q4f-2026-03 landed in staging and we're seeing streaming cutoffs when the model emits two consecutive EOS-like tokens. Repro: start a long chat, model emits '</s>' twice and the stream closes early. Anyone seen this? :thinking:

sam: hmm, haven't seen double-EOS before. Do you have logs? is it deterministic? :eyes:

lina: pretty deterministic for a few prompts. quick tail from staging stream:

```
STREAM_OUT token=50256 text="</s>" reason=stop
STREAM_OUT token=1 text="</s>" reason=stop
STREAM_CLOSE code=200 reason="stop_sequence"
```

After that the client sometimes reconnects and gets the remainder (weird), sometimes nothing.

ow digging into tokenizer/config mismatch: the HF tokenizer we converted returns '' but the model config had `eos_token: "</s>"`. During quantize+convert we ended up with both string and token-id stop checks.

ow experimenting with a quick workaround: normalize stops to tokenizer.eos_token id before serving. Example snippet we tried: 

```python
# normalize stop sequences to a single string
stops = chat_template.get("stop_sequences", [])
stops = [tokenizer.eos_token if s in ("", "</s>") else s for s in stops]
chat_template["stop_sequences"] = stops
```

That reduced occurrences but didn't eliminate it when model emits repeated EOS ids (consecutive tokens).

ow hypothesis: runtime treats first EOS as complete and drops remaining token buffers leading to rare data truncation. Could be in the streaming buffer flush path where multiple stop detections race with KV cache flush.

ow some quick checks: 
- jitted runtime checks for stop_token string vs token id both present?
- quantization path may remap eos token id (50256 vs 1 difference seen above)
- chat template had newline + '' as stops which map to different tokenization splits

ow logs from a failing trace (truncated ids): 

```
[2026-03-18T14:03:12Z] generate_chunk seq=480 tokens=24 last_token=50256
[2026-03-18T14:03:12Z] detect_stop token_id=50256 -> closing stream
[2026-03-18T14:03:12Z] emit_buffer flush size=128
[2026-03-18T14:03:12Z] detect_stop token_id=1 -> ignored (stream already closed)
```

ow questions: should runtime coalesce consecutive stop detections and only close after draining buffer? or treat repeated EOS as a single stop but still emit buffer content?

ow what I changed in canary for testing: normalized chat template stops and added a tiny delay (15ms) before final stream close to let emit_buffer flush. that reduced reconnects but is obviously a hack.

ow owen: I can reproduce on GPU-A with q4f build. repro script will be in the ticket. appears more likely when response token length > ~400 and when model was converted with HF tokenizers that had dual-EOS entries.

jess: filing internal bug with reproducer + logs. tagging runtime + convert teams. link: https://redwood.internal/issue/MLINF-2742 :+1:

deploy-bot: rolled canary q4f-2026-03 to 10% in staging for testing

sam: thanks. next steps: (1) add a normalization step in HF->Redwood converter that collapses duplicate EOS tokens and aligns token ids, (2) update runtime to buffer+drain before final close when stop detected, (3) add an e2e test that streams multi-eos sequences from converted models. anyone want ownership for (1)?

lina: I'll take (1) and drop a PR today. will also attach tokenizer samples.

ow jess: I'll own the e2e test. owen can you coordinate runtime changes with eng-runtime?

ow short-term mitigation: add canonicalization in serving path and disable immediate stream close until drain finished. long-term fix needs runtime patch.

sam: great — keep updates in the ticket. thanks for catching this early, lina. :clap:
